set.overview: Chair Peak's northeast buttress, at the head of the Alpental valley above Snoqualmie Pass, is a winter mixed climb: four pitches of snow, ice and easy rock, with the crux a short ice bulge on the third.
set.beta: From the basin below Chair Peak's East Face, the route climbs a curving gully system on climber's right before trending up and left along the buttress crest to the summit. The technical crux in winter conditions is a short, steep ice bulge encountered partway up. It is commonly done in 4 pitches with a 60m rope, though many parties simul-climb sections or break it into 5-6 shorter pitches, especially in early-season snow. Short approach and moderate climbing make it very popular and prone to queues on clear winter weekends.
